Reclamation is safe because evidence only exists upon pairing an intent record with a completion certificate in the durable log.","counterconditions":[{"case":"An acknowledged completion certificate write may be lost due to a subsequent log corruption","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Timestamp or sequence ordering failures may pair an intent with the wrong certificate","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A workspace may contain evidence that is valid but not yet certified at crash time","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Before computation, the process appends an intent record (problem_id, input_hash, lease_nonce) to a strongly durable, single-writer append-only log. The workspace itself is treated as weakly durable scratch. Upon completion, an immutable evidence artifact is written to a separate strongly durable store, and a completion certificate is appended to the intent log. The protocol durably records the intent log and all completion certificates. A crash leaves an unpaired intent; the scratch workspace may be reclaimed immediately because the absence of a completion certificate proves no evidence was durably completed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
